metin: For decades, economists assumed that people make financial decisions rationally, carefully weighing costs and benefits. Behavioural economics has challenged this view by showing that emotions and mental shortcuts strongly influence our choices. For instance, people are often more upset by losing a sum of money than they are pleased by gaining the same amount. Governments now use such insights to design policies that gently steer citizens towards better decisions.
dogru: Research shows that people's financial decisions are less rational than once thought, and this knowledge is now used in policy.
celdiriciler: Behavioural economics proves that people always make perfectly rational choices.
Governments have stopped using economic research when designing policies.
People are usually happier about gains than they are upset about equal losses.

metin: Remote villages in many countries are losing their populations as young people move to cities in search of work. Some regions have responded by offering incentives, such as cheap housing or grants for new businesses, to attract newcomers. The results have been mixed: a few villages have been revived, while others have seen people leave again once the support ended. Experts argue that reliable internet and public services matter more than one-off payments.
dogru: Efforts to repopulate villages have had mixed results, and lasting infrastructure seems more important than short-term incentives.
celdiriciler: Young people are leaving cities to live in remote villages in large numbers.
Offering cheap housing has revived every village that tried it.
Experts believe one-off payments are the most effective way to keep people in villages.

metin: Sleep researchers have found that teenagers' body clocks naturally shift later during adolescence, making it difficult for them to fall asleep early. Nevertheless, most schools start early in the morning, which means many students are chronically tired. Some schools that moved their start time by an hour reported better attendance and improved concentration. Critics, however, point to practical problems such as bus schedules and parents' working hours.
dogru: Later school start times may suit teenagers' biology better, though they raise practical difficulties.
celdiriciler: Teenagers naturally prefer to go to bed and wake up very early.
Moving school start times later has made students more tired.
Nobody sees any practical problems with changing school hours.

metin: When Leyla took over her father's small textile factory, orders were falling and the machines were outdated. Rather than competing on price with large manufacturers, she decided to focus on high-quality, sustainably produced fabrics. It took three difficult years and a large bank loan, but the business now exports to several European countries. Leyla believes that the crisis forced her to rethink everything and ultimately made the company stronger.
dogru: By changing the company's focus, Leyla turned a struggling factory into a successful exporter.
celdiriciler: Leyla sold her father's factory because it was losing money.
Leyla succeeded by producing cheaper fabrics than large manufacturers.
The factory has never had financial difficulties.

metin: Plastic pollution in the oceans has received enormous media attention, and rightly so. However, some scientists warn that focusing only on plastic straws and bags may distract from larger sources of damage, such as abandoned fishing nets and industrial waste. They argue that consumer choices, while useful, cannot replace strong regulation of industry. Both individual and collective action, they say, are needed.
dogru: Scientists warn that tackling ocean pollution requires regulating industry, not only changing consumer habits.
celdiriciler: Scientists say that banning plastic straws will solve ocean pollution.
Media attention to ocean plastic has been completely unjustified.
Fishing nets and industrial waste cause little damage to the oceans.

metin: Many companies now use algorithms to screen job applications before a human ever reads them. Supporters claim that this saves time and reduces the influence of personal bias. Yet several studies have found that such systems can reproduce existing inequalities, because they learn from past hiring decisions that were themselves biased. Some countries are now considering laws that would require these tools to be tested for fairness.
dogru: Automated hiring tools save time but may repeat past discrimination, which has led to calls for regulation.
celdiriciler: Algorithms have completely eliminated bias from hiring.
Companies have stopped using software to screen applications.
Studies show that algorithms always make fairer decisions than humans.

metin: Language learners often worry about their accent and feel embarrassed when native speakers notice it. Linguists, however, emphasise that intelligibility, not a perfect accent, is what matters for communication. Most listeners have no difficulty understanding a speaker with a foreign accent as long as key sounds and word stress are clear. Focusing on these features is therefore more useful than trying to sound exactly like a native speaker.
dogru: Being clearly understood matters more than having a native-like accent.
celdiriciler: Learners must lose their accent completely to be understood.
Native speakers usually cannot understand people with foreign accents.
Word stress has no effect on how well a speaker is understood.

metin: The rise of streaming services has transformed how films are made and watched. Studios increasingly release films directly online, and audiences can watch them at home on the day of release. While this is convenient, cinema owners fear for their future, and some directors argue that films lose part of their impact on a small screen. Others believe cinemas will survive by offering experiences that cannot be reproduced at home.
dogru: Streaming has changed the film industry, raising concerns about cinemas while some expect them to adapt.
celdiriciler: Streaming services have had no effect on the film industry.
All directors prefer their films to be watched on small screens.
Cinemas have already disappeared because of streaming.

metin: After years of commuting two hours a day, Murat and his partner moved from Istanbul to a small coastal town. Their income fell because Murat had to accept a lower-paid local job, but their living costs also dropped considerably. More importantly, they now have time to cook, exercise and see friends during the week. They admit that they sometimes miss the cultural life of the city, but they do not regret the decision.
dogru: Moving to a small town reduced the couple's income but improved their quality of life.
celdiriciler: Murat earns much more money since moving to the coast.
The couple regrets leaving Istanbul and plans to return.
Murat and his partner still commute two hours a day.

metin: Antibiotics are among the most important medical discoveries of the last century. Yet their overuse, both in human medicine and in farming, has allowed bacteria to develop resistance. Infections that were once easy to treat are becoming dangerous again in some parts of the world. Health organisations are urging doctors to prescribe antibiotics only when truly necessary and farmers to stop using them to make animals grow faster.
dogru: The overuse of antibiotics is creating resistant bacteria, so their use needs to be limited.
celdiriciler: Antibiotics are no longer used in medicine or farming.
Bacteria cannot develop resistance to antibiotics.
Health organisations recommend using more antibiotics in farming.

metin: Public libraries have had to reinvent themselves in the digital age. Alongside books, many now offer free internet access, language classes, help with job applications and even spaces where people can use 3D printers. For people without computers at home, these services are essential. Some librarians describe their buildings as the last public places where anyone can spend time without having to buy something.
dogru: Libraries have adapted by offering many services beyond books, especially for people who need them.
celdiriciler: Libraries have stopped lending books in the digital age.
Most people no longer need any services from libraries.
Libraries now charge visitors to spend time inside.

metin: It is commonly believed that multitasking allows us to get more done. Research suggests the opposite: when we switch between tasks, our brains need time to refocus, and errors increase. What feels like doing two things at once is usually rapid switching, which is tiring and inefficient. Experts recommend grouping similar tasks and working on one thing at a time for set periods.
dogru: Multitasking tends to reduce efficiency, so focusing on one task at a time is recommended.
celdiriciler: Research proves that multitasking increases productivity.
Switching between tasks makes people make fewer mistakes.
Experts advise doing as many tasks as possible at the same moment.

metin: In several European cities, old industrial areas have been turned into creative districts full of studios, cafés and small businesses. At first, these changes brought life to neglected neighbourhoods. Over time, however, rising property prices pushed out many of the artists and residents who had made the areas attractive in the first place. This process, known as gentrification, is now a central topic in urban planning debates.
dogru: Regenerating old industrial areas can improve them but may also force original residents out.
celdiriciler: Old industrial areas are always left empty and neglected.
Rising property prices help artists stay in creative districts.
Urban planners are not interested in gentrification.

metin: Volunteer firefighters make up the majority of fire services in many rural areas. They train in their free time and leave their regular jobs whenever an alarm sounds. In recent years, however, it has become harder to recruit new volunteers, as young people move away and employers are less willing to let staff leave work. Some regions are considering paying volunteers a small fee to keep the system working.
dogru: Rural fire services rely on volunteers, but recruiting them is becoming increasingly difficult.
celdiriciler: Rural areas are protected mainly by full-time professional firefighters.
More young people than ever are joining volunteer fire services.
Employers are happy to let volunteers leave work at any time.

metin: Handwriting is disappearing from many classrooms as students type more of their work. Some researchers argue that this is a loss, because writing by hand appears to help students remember information better than typing. When we write by hand, we cannot copy every word, so we are forced to summarise and process ideas. Others respond that typing skills are more useful in the modern world.
dogru: Some researchers believe handwriting aids learning, although others value typing more.
celdiriciler: Research shows that typing helps students remember more than handwriting.
Handwriting is becoming more common in classrooms.
Everyone agrees that handwriting is no longer useful.

metin: The small island had depended on fishing for centuries, but declining fish stocks threatened the local economy. Instead of expanding tourism on a large scale, the community chose to develop small guesthouses run by local families and to protect the surrounding waters as a marine reserve. Fish numbers have slowly recovered, and visitors now come specifically to dive in the protected area.
dogru: An island community protected its waters and developed small-scale tourism to save its economy.
celdiriciler: The island built large hotels to replace fishing.
Fish stocks around the island continue to decline sharply.
Tourists are not allowed to visit the protected area.

metin: Loneliness is increasingly recognised as a public health issue rather than simply a personal problem. Studies link long-term loneliness to higher risks of heart disease and depression. In response, some countries have appointed ministers responsible for tackling loneliness, and doctors can refer patients to social activities rather than prescribing medication. Critics wonder, however, whether governments can really solve such a personal experience.
dogru: Loneliness is being treated as a health issue, although some question what governments can achieve.
celdiriciler: Studies show that loneliness has no effect on physical health.
Doctors are now forbidden from recommending social activities.
All critics agree that governments can easily end loneliness.

metin: Many people buy bottled water because they believe it is safer than tap water. In most developed countries, however, tap water is tested more frequently and meets stricter standards than bottled water. Bottled water is also far more expensive and creates large amounts of plastic waste. Campaigners are therefore encouraging people to carry refillable bottles instead.
dogru: In many countries tap water is safe, making bottled water an expensive and wasteful choice.
celdiriciler: Bottled water is tested more strictly than tap water everywhere.
Tap water is usually more expensive than bottled water.
Campaigners encourage people to buy more bottled water.

metin: When the new manager arrived, the team was demotivated and several people were planning to leave. Instead of introducing major changes immediately, she spent her first month listening to each employee's concerns. She then removed some unnecessary meetings and gave staff more freedom to organise their work. Within a year, staff turnover had dropped significantly.
dogru: By listening first and then making targeted changes, the new manager improved the team's morale.
celdiriciler: The new manager introduced strict rules on her first day.
More employees left the team after the manager arrived.
The manager added more meetings to control the team.

metin: The price of a product often tells us less about its quality than we think. Experiments have shown that people rate the same wine as tastier when they are told it is expensive. Marketing experts use this effect to position products as premium, even when production costs are similar to cheaper brands. Consumers who compare ingredients or reviews can often save money without losing quality.
dogru: Price influences how we judge quality, so comparing products carefully can save money.
celdiriciler: Expensive products are always of higher quality than cheap ones.
People's taste is never influenced by price.
Marketing experts try to make premium products look cheap.

metin: Glaciers in the Alps have been shrinking rapidly over the past few decades. Apart from the loss of spectacular landscapes, this has practical consequences: many rivers depend on meltwater during the summer, and hydroelectric power stations rely on a steady water supply. Scientists estimate that most Alpine glaciers could disappear by the end of the century if current trends continue.
dogru: The rapid melting of Alpine glaciers threatens both landscapes and water-dependent activities.
celdiriciler: Alpine glaciers have been growing over recent decades.
Rivers in the Alps do not depend on glacier meltwater.
Scientists expect glaciers to stay the same size this century.

metin: At sixteen, Kaan was more interested in computer games than in school. A teacher noticed that he was good at solving puzzles in games and suggested he join the programming club. Kaan soon discovered he enjoyed creating games even more than playing them. He is now studying computer science and has already published two small games of his own.
dogru: A teacher helped Kaan turn his interest in games into a passion for programming.
celdiriciler: Kaan stopped playing games to concentrate on school.
Kaan's teacher told him to give up computer games completely.
Kaan is studying to become a teacher.

metin: Supermarkets throw away large amounts of food that is still perfectly edible, often because it has reached its sell-by date or does not look perfect. Several countries have introduced laws requiring large shops to donate such food to charities instead of destroying it. Apps have also appeared that allow customers to buy surplus food at a discount at the end of the day.
dogru: Laws and apps are being used to reduce the amount of edible food that supermarkets waste.
celdiriciler: Supermarkets rarely throw away any food.
New laws require supermarkets to destroy food after its sell-by date.
Apps are used to sell supermarket food at higher prices.

metin: It is often said that we only use ten per cent of our brains. This idea appears in films and advertisements, but neuroscientists have repeatedly shown it to be false. Brain scans reveal that almost all areas of the brain are active at some point during the day, even during sleep. The myth probably survives because it suggests that we all have hidden potential waiting to be unlocked.
dogru: The popular belief that we use only ten per cent of our brains is a myth.
celdiriciler: Neuroscientists have confirmed that we use only a small part of our brains.
The brain is completely inactive during sleep.
Films and advertisements have stopped repeating the ten per cent idea.

metin: Car-sharing schemes allow members to book a vehicle for a few hours using an app. For people who drive only occasionally, this can be much cheaper than owning a car, since they do not pay for insurance, parking or repairs. Cities also benefit because each shared car can replace several private ones. However, the schemes work best in dense areas and are less practical in the countryside.
dogru: Car-sharing can save money and space in cities but is less suitable for rural areas.
celdiriciler: Car-sharing is always more expensive than owning a car.
Car-sharing schemes work best in the countryside.
Shared cars increase the number of cars in cities.

metin: The festival started twenty years ago as a small gathering of local musicians in a farmer's field. Today it attracts more than fifty thousand visitors and international stars. While the organisers are proud of this success, residents have begun to complain about traffic, noise and litter. The town council is now negotiating limits on the number of tickets and new rules for waste management.
dogru: A festival's growth has brought success but also problems that the town is now trying to manage.
celdiriciler: The festival has become smaller over the past twenty years.
Residents are fully satisfied with the festival's growth.
The council has decided to cancel the festival permanently.

metin: Many parents worry that video games are harmful to children. Research paints a more complex picture. While excessive gaming can affect sleep and schoolwork, moderate play has been linked to improved problem-solving skills and teamwork, especially in games that require cooperation. Experts suggest that parents pay attention to the type of game and the amount of time spent rather than banning games altogether.
dogru: The effects of video games depend on how much and what kind of games children play.
celdiriciler: Research proves that all video games are harmful to children.
Experts recommend banning video games completely.
Moderate gaming has no benefits at all.

metin: Traditional crafts such as carpet weaving and copper work are disappearing in many regions because young people see little future in them. Some organisations are trying to reverse this trend by connecting craftspeople directly with online buyers around the world. This allows artisans to earn fair prices without depending on middlemen. As a result, a small number of young people have started to learn these skills again.
dogru: Selling crafts online is helping to keep some traditional skills alive.
celdiriciler: Traditional crafts are more popular than ever among young people.
Online sales have made artisans more dependent on middlemen.
Organisations are trying to replace crafts with factory production.

metin: Sara had been a successful lawyer for ten years when she realised she no longer enjoyed her work. Despite the financial risk, she enrolled in a teacher training programme at the age of thirty-eight. The first year of teaching was exhausting, and she earned far less than before. Still, she says she feels, for the first time in years, that her work has meaning.
dogru: Sara left a well-paid legal career for teaching and found more meaningful work.
celdiriciler: Sara became a lawyer after working as a teacher.
Sara earns more as a teacher than she did as a lawyer.
Sara regrets leaving her job as a lawyer.

metin: Urban trees do much more than make streets look pleasant. They provide shade, lower temperatures during heatwaves, absorb rainwater and filter pollutants from the air. Studies even suggest that people living near green spaces report better mental health. Despite these benefits, trees are often cut down during construction projects because they are seen as an obstacle.
dogru: City trees have many benefits, yet they are often removed during construction.
celdiriciler: Urban trees are mainly useful for decoration.
Trees raise temperatures in cities during heatwaves.
Construction projects usually plant more trees than they remove.

metin: The idea of a universal basic income, a regular payment given to every citizen regardless of their situation, has been tested in several countries. Supporters argue that it provides security and allows people to retrain or start businesses. Opponents fear it would be too expensive and might discourage people from working. So far, the trials have been too small and short to settle the debate.
dogru: Universal basic income has been trialled, but the evidence is not yet enough to settle the debate.
celdiriciler: Universal basic income has been introduced permanently in every country.
Trials have proved that basic income stops people from working.
Supporters and opponents agree that basic income is too expensive.

metin: Before a major exam, many students try to memorise as much information as possible the night before. Cognitive scientists recommend a different approach called spaced practice, in which material is reviewed several times over days or weeks. Although it feels less productive at the time, spacing out study sessions leads to much better long-term memory. Testing yourself regularly is another effective strategy.
dogru: Reviewing material over time is more effective for memory than last-minute cramming.
celdiriciler: Studying everything the night before is the best strategy.
Spaced practice feels very productive but does not help memory.
Testing yourself makes it harder to remember information.

metin: The discovery of a Roman mosaic under a car park surprised both archaeologists and local residents. Construction work was immediately stopped so that experts could study the site. The developers were initially frustrated by the delay, but they eventually agreed to redesign the building so that the mosaic could be displayed to the public on the ground floor.
dogru: An unexpected archaeological find led developers to change their building plans.
celdiriciler: The Roman mosaic was destroyed to build a car park.
Archaeologists were not interested in the mosaic.
The developers refused to change their plans.

metin: Social media platforms make money mainly by selling advertising. The longer users stay on a platform, the more adverts they see, so the apps are designed to capture as much attention as possible. Features such as endless scrolling and constant notifications are not accidental. Some former employees of tech companies have become vocal critics of these design choices.
dogru: Social media apps are deliberately designed to keep users' attention because it earns them money.
celdiriciler: Social media platforms make most of their money from user subscriptions.
Endless scrolling was added to apps by accident.
No one who has worked in the tech industry has criticised these designs.

metin: Many people assume that introverts dislike other people. In fact, psychologists describe introversion mainly in terms of energy: introverts tend to feel drained after long periods of social activity and recharge by spending time alone. They can be excellent communicators and often prefer deep conversations with a few friends to large gatherings. Understanding this difference can help teams work better together.
dogru: Introversion is about how people gain energy, not a dislike of others.
celdiriciler: Introverts generally dislike people and avoid all conversations.
Introverts gain energy from large social gatherings.
Psychologists say introverts cannot be good communicators.

metin: Last spring, a local bakery began paying its suppliers more for flour grown without pesticides. This raised the price of bread by a small amount, and the owner expected to lose customers. Instead, sales increased, partly because customers appreciated knowing where their food came from. The bakery now organises visits to the farms that supply it.
dogru: A bakery's switch to more expensive, sustainable flour unexpectedly increased its sales.
celdiriciler: The bakery lost most of its customers after raising prices.
The bakery started using cheaper flour to lower prices.
Customers were not interested in where their bread came from.

metin: Space agencies are increasingly concerned about space debris, the thousands of pieces of old satellites and rockets orbiting the Earth. Travelling at enormous speeds, even a tiny fragment can seriously damage a working satellite. As more private companies launch satellites, the risk of collisions grows. Engineers are developing ways to capture debris or make satellites burn up safely at the end of their lives.
dogru: Growing amounts of space debris pose a risk, and engineers are working on solutions.
celdiriciler: Space debris moves too slowly to cause any damage.
Fewer satellites are being launched now than in the past.
Engineers believe nothing can be done about space debris.

metin: After losing his job at fifty-five, Ahmet struggled to find new work because employers preferred younger candidates. Rather than giving up, he took an online course in bookkeeping and offered his services to small local businesses. His years of experience in management turned out to be a real advantage. Two years later, he employs three people.
dogru: After losing his job, Ahmet retrained and built a successful small business.
celdiriciler: Ahmet retired after he lost his job.
Employers were eager to hire Ahmet because of his age.
Ahmet's previous experience was useless in his new work.

metin: The four-day school week has been adopted by some rural schools in the United States, mainly to save money on transport and heating. Surprisingly, teachers in these schools report higher job satisfaction, and some districts find it easier to recruit staff. However, studies on student achievement show mixed results, and families sometimes struggle to arrange childcare on the extra day off.
dogru: A four-day school week saves money and pleases teachers, but its effects on students and families are mixed.
celdiriciler: All schools in the United States now have a four-day week.
The four-day week has clearly improved student achievement everywhere.
Teachers in these schools are less satisfied with their jobs.

metin: Photographs have long been considered reliable evidence of what really happened. With modern editing software and artificial intelligence, however, it has become easy to create images that look completely real but show events that never took place. Journalists now use special tools to check the origin of pictures before publishing them. Readers, too, are advised to be cautious about images shared without a clear source.
dogru: Because realistic fake images are now easy to create, photos can no longer be trusted automatically.
celdiriciler: Artificial intelligence has made it impossible to edit photographs.
Journalists publish all images without checking them.
Photographs are more reliable evidence today than ever before.

metin: In many cultures, the main meal of the day was traditionally eaten together by the whole family. Busy work schedules, long commutes and individual screen time have made this less common. Nutritionists and psychologists alike point out that shared meals are associated with healthier eating and stronger family relationships. Some families now aim for just a few shared meals a week rather than none at all.
dogru: Family meals have become less common, although they are linked to health and closer relationships.
celdiriciler: Families eat together more often now than in the past.
Shared meals are associated with unhealthy eating.
Experts advise families to stop eating together.

metin: Electric scooters appeared on city streets almost overnight and quickly divided public opinion. Users praise them as a cheap, fun way to travel short distances. Pedestrians, however, complain about scooters being ridden on pavements and left blocking the way. Several cities have responded by setting speed limits, creating parking zones and, in some cases, banning rental scooters altogether.
dogru: Electric scooters are popular but controversial, leading cities to introduce new rules.
celdiriciler: Everyone agrees that electric scooters improve city life.
Cities have encouraged scooter users to ride on pavements.
Electric scooters have been in cities for many decades.

metin: Zehra always found public speaking terrifying, which became a problem when she was promoted to a position that required regular presentations. She joined a club where members practise speaking in front of each other and give constructive feedback. Although she still feels nervous, she has learned techniques to control her anxiety. Her colleagues now say her presentations are among the clearest in the company.
dogru: Practising in a supportive club helped Zehra manage her fear of public speaking.
celdiriciler: Zehra refused a promotion because it required presentations.
Zehra no longer feels nervous at all when speaking.
Zehra's colleagues think her presentations are unclear.

metin: Rewilding is an approach to conservation that aims to restore natural processes rather than manage every detail of a landscape. It can involve reintroducing animals such as beavers or wolves that once lived in an area. Beavers, for instance, build dams that create wetlands, which in turn support many other species. Farmers, however, sometimes worry about damage to their land and livestock.
dogru: Rewilding restores natural processes, sometimes by bringing back species, although farmers may have concerns.
celdiriciler: Rewilding means controlling every part of a landscape carefully.
Beavers destroy wetlands and harm other species.
Farmers are always enthusiastic about reintroducing wolves.

metin: The company promised customers that its new phone would last a whole day on a single charge. Within weeks of its release, however, users reported that the battery ran out by early afternoon. The company first blamed users' settings, but independent tests confirmed the problem. Eventually it offered free replacements and a public apology, which partly restored its reputation.
dogru: A company eventually admitted a battery problem and tried to repair its reputation.
celdiriciler: The phone's battery lasted much longer than promised.
Independent tests showed that users' settings caused the problem.
The company refused to replace any phones.

metin: Minimalism, the idea of owning fewer possessions, has become popular through books and online videos. Its supporters say that having less makes life simpler, reduces stress and saves money. Critics note, however, that minimalism is often presented as a lifestyle choice for wealthy people, who can easily replace things when needed. For people on low incomes, keeping items for future use may be a practical necessity.
dogru: Minimalism appeals to many, but critics say it is easier to practise for wealthier people.
celdiriciler: Minimalism encourages people to buy as many possessions as possible.
Critics say minimalism is especially suitable for people on low incomes.
Nobody has written books or made videos about minimalism.

metin: In the nineteenth century, most people lived their entire lives within a short distance of where they were born. The arrival of the railway changed this dramatically. Suddenly it was possible to visit the seaside for a day or move to a city for work. The railway also led to the standardisation of time, because timetables required every town to use the same clock.
dogru: The railway transformed people's mobility and even the way time was measured.
celdiriciler: The railway made travel slower and more difficult.
Towns kept their own local times after the railway arrived.
Most people in the nineteenth century travelled widely before railways.

metin: Many universities now record their lectures and make them available online. Students appreciate being able to watch difficult parts again or catch up after illness. Some lecturers, however, have noticed that attendance falls when recordings are available. Research suggests that students who rely only on recordings and rarely attend in person tend to perform worse.
dogru: Recorded lectures are useful, but relying on them entirely may harm students' results.
celdiriciler: Universities have stopped recording lectures.
Attendance increases when lectures are recorded.
Students who only watch recordings perform better than others.

metin: When a large supermarket opened on the edge of town, several small grocery shops in the centre closed within two years. The shops that survived did so by offering something the supermarket could not: personal service, local products and home delivery for older customers. One shop owner says that knowing her customers by name has been her greatest advantage.
dogru: Small shops survived competition from a supermarket by offering personal, local services.
celdiriciler: All the small shops in the town centre closed.
The small shops competed by lowering their prices below the supermarket's.
The supermarket closed because customers preferred small shops.

metin: The human voice reveals more than just words. Listeners can often guess a speaker's mood, age and even whether they are telling the truth from the tone of voice alone. Researchers are now training computer programs to detect such signals, for example to identify early signs of illness. The technology raises privacy concerns, however, since voices can be recorded without people's knowledge.
dogru: Voices carry a lot of information, and new technology to analyse them brings both benefits and privacy concerns.
celdiriciler: The tone of a voice gives no information about a speaker's mood.
Computer programs cannot analyse human voices.
Voice analysis technology raises no privacy issues.
